facts.text: ThanksKilling's famous tagline, "Gobble, gobble, motherf*cker!", was dreamed up by creators Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart before they had any actual plot.
Pilgrim girl Wanda Lust was cast off Craigslist, and was the only actor paid. The adult film performer later said it was the one film credit she regrets.
Director Jordan Downey wanted a much bigger opening with a full Pilgrim and Native American dinner, but time and money ran out. It was never shot.
The whole movie cost about $3,500 and was shot in roughly two weeks in summer 2007 by college students Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart.
The nude Pilgrim opening was shot in a public park without a permit. Many locations were chosen because they needed none.
The film was shot during the summer between Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart's junior and senior years at college, and partly at Denison University in Granville, Ohio.
Writers Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart came up with ideas by walking to a nearby Blockbuster and studying the covers of bad movies.
Before settling on a Thanksgiving slasher, Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart considered an Easter slasher called "Eggstravakill".
Auditions were held in director Jordan Downey's garage. Cast members were mostly friends and family.
Ryan E. Francis (Darren) drums in the band Overated, whose song "The Lines Have Been Drawn" plays on the radio during the Jeep ride.
Lindsey Anderson (Kristen) joined on Ryan E. Francis's recommendation. The filmmakers met her at a doughnut shop days before shooting began.
Director Jordan Downey sculpted the Turkie puppet in his apartment bathroom, using leftover effects supplies and a foam turkey hunting decoy as the body.
Effects artist Troy Smith's gore budget was only a few hundred dollars. The blood work reportedly leaned on cheap materials, including strawberry jam.
The filmmakers never found a name for the killer turkey in 2008. For the 2012 sequel they finally settled on "Turkie".
Hermit actor General Bastard drove in from Michigan to shoot his scenes over a few days.
The magic totem was bought on eBay. It arrived only a few inches tall, so the filmmakers embraced the absurdity and used it anyway.
The only footage shot but cut was an improvised dream scene in which Darren runs through a cornfield. There are no other deleted scenes.
The turkey's feet and lower half are never seen in the film.
Actor Chuck Lamb's faceless sheriff look came from a fake fleshy mask made by effects artist Troy Smith.
Wondering about the continuity? The campus scenes show autumn leaves, but the film was shot in summer, so the woods are green.
The film nearly went to Troma, but the filmmakers pulled out and sold DVDs themselves on Amazon. It took about a year to sell 1,000 copies.
Director Jordan Downey credits Netflix and the distributor Gravitas Ventures with helping the film find its cult audience after the slow self-distributed DVD start.
The first public screening was at the Merry Scary Winter Horrorland festival, part of the Sacramento Horror Fest, in December 2008.
Director Jordan Downey on why he made it: "There was no reason to make it other than to have fun and I do think that shines through."
Reviews were mixed. Tom Russo of The Boston Globe called it "cheerily awful", while Forbes' Mark Hughes said it is so awful it doesn't need MST3K-style jokes to entertain.
The "To be continued in space..." card was a pure joke. Even so, ThanksKilling 3 followed in 2012, skipping a "2" on purpose; its plot is the hunt for the lost middle film.
The 2012 sequel ThanksKilling 3 raised $112,248 on Kickstarter, about thirty times the original's $3,500 budget.
ThanksKilling: The Musical premiered in Seattle in 2013. Ryan E. Francis, who plays Darren in the film, later reprised the role on stage in Columbus, Ohio.
The musical's producer David Eck first watched the film on a plane. Its writers reportedly produced the script in about three days after meeting Jordan Downey and Kevin Stewart.
The filmmakers copyrighted "Death Turkey" as an alternate title for overseas markets that don't celebrate Thanksgiving.
